common_name: Queen of the Night Tulip (Deep Maroon-Black Single Late Tulip)

planting.note: Plant bulbs in fall six to eight inches deep in well-drained soil; Queen of the Night is the deep maroon-black heirloom tulip whose fully double sport 'Black Hero' inherits this same near-black color.

directions: Queen of the Night is the archetypal 'black' tulip, a Single Late selection introduced from the Netherlands in 1944 that opens deep, velvety maroon-purple blooms so dark they read as black in shade and glow burgundy in direct sun. Its tall, sturdy stems hold the goblet-shaped flowers well above the foliage in late spring, making it a dramatic anchor in borders planted for moody color schemes or contrasted with pale apricot, white, or lime-green companions. It has since given rise to sports such as the fully double 'Black Hero'. Plant bulbs in fall in well-drained soil in full sun, and allow the foliage to yellow and die back naturally after bloom before removing it.
